title: Killers of the Flower moon ---- Scene interpretation question

commenti.body:
I think they are just bystanders looking, scorsese planting the idea of whitenesses of their relationship, potentially suspecting, and also underlining perhaps  the apathy of white people around these murders.

I also dont see what defines them as divine, theres no "tell" to indicate this, also god or religion as a concept is barely touched in the movie (apart from the osage customs shown)

yes that could be the case. i wonder why they stopped working to just stare at two strangers seemingly going about their business. And they stare with such blankness.

Your right there is not a hint of religion in the movie, which makes this scene so interesting to me.  Because its out of character of the movie for there to be anything surreal.  And this seems to be a hint of the surreal  ( if its interpreted that they arent real people) 

And if it is symbolic, its basically the only case of that aside from the owl scenes, which the movie is basically explicit in saying the owl isnt really there
there is the scene where the mother goes with her ancestor in the fields and we see she died...so, there is at least one religious (or mystic) scene

God was mentioned many many times in this film repeatedly by just about every main character and personally I think the presence of god (or some divine being like the Owl) is primary theme in this film so I don't think it's a stretch to say these oil workers were a metaphorical representation of god silently watching over the crimes. My first thought was that they represented the apathy of the average white folk to the murders in the area who knew what was happening but didn't think much of it because they Indian.
